---
title: "Code Walkthrough"
subtitle: "The cmg planner one layer at a time: commands to run, the output they printed, why, and exercises with solutions."
---

`cmg` is the reference implementation of [Planning Through Contact](../index.qmd): a
contact-formation search for the box-over-a-step task, built on JAX, Equinox,
MuJoCo-MJX and MPAX. This walkthrough runs it layer by layer, from the scene file
up to the search loop. Every page gives a command, the script (folded), the
output it printed, what to notice in that output, where to read the code, and a
few exercises with folded solutions.

It studies the code **as it is**, including its known problems; several pages
end on a defect that the next stage of the project fixes. The last page,
[Where step 1 starts](09-step1.qmd), collects them.

**Code version.** Angelo's branch `phase1/dev` at commit `7d2d343`
(2026-11-04). `phase1/aykut` matches it except for the search save/load added in
the last five commits, which only step 8 uses.

## Setup

The setup commands come in a bash and a fish version; pick the tab for your
shell (the choice applies to both blocks below).

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## bash

```bash
cd ~/repos/research/c-gnn              # your clone of Symplectomorphism/c-gnn
git fetch origin
git switch --detach origin/phase1/dev  # 7d2d343, the commit used here
cd cmg
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]" matplotlib
```

## fish

```sh
cd ~/repos/research/c-gnn              # your clone of Symplectomorphism/c-gnn
git fetch origin
git switch --detach origin/phase1/dev  # 7d2d343, the commit used here
cd cmg
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
source .venv/bin/activate.fish
uv pip install -e ".[dev]" matplotlib
```
:::

The install takes a minute or two. Then fetch the walkthrough scripts into
`cmg/walkthrough/` and keep that folder out of git:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## bash

```bash
mkdir -p walkthrough && cd walkthrough
base=https://symplectomorphism.github.io/research/nonprehensile/code-walkthrough/scripts
for f in _common.py 01_scene.py 02_templates.py 03_formations.py 04_graph.py \
         05_hold.py 06_candidates.py 07_mppi.py 08_search.py 08b_search_rounds.py replay.py; do
  curl -fsSLO "$base/$f"
done
cd ..
echo "walkthrough/" >> ../.git/info/exclude
```

## fish

```sh
mkdir -p walkthrough; and cd walkthrough
set base https://symplectomorphism.github.io/research/nonprehensile/code-walkthrough/scripts
for f in _common.py 01_scene.py 02_templates.py 03_formations.py 04_graph.py \
         05_hold.py 06_candidates.py 07_mppi.py 08_search.py 08b_search_rounds.py replay.py
    curl -fsSLO "$base/$f"
end
cd ..
echo "walkthrough/" >> ../.git/info/exclude
```
:::

Every command on the following pages runs from `cmg/` with the virtual
environment active, and is the same in bash and fish (fish 3.1 or newer
accepts the `VAR=value command` form used below). In a new terminal, activate
the environment again with `source .venv/bin/activate` (bash) or
`source .venv/bin/activate.fish` (fish). The scripts are also linked on each page.

When you are done with the walkthrough, return your clone to your branch with
`git switch <your-branch>` from the repository root (run `git status` first;
`git restore .` discards any edits the exercises made to tracked files).

**Baseline: the test suite.**

```bash
PYTHONPATH=tests python -m pytest -q tests
```

```text
......                                                                   [100%]
6 passed, 2 warnings in 97.70s (0:01:37)
```

`PYTHONPATH=tests` is needed because two tests import a helper module from
`tests/`. Only four of the nine test files contain tests that pytest collects.
`test_relocate`, `test_markgraph_structure`, `test_gap_greedy_misses` and
`test_horiz_support` are placeholders. `test_local_solver` is a hand-run script
(everything is under `if __name__ == "__main__"`), and it reads a
`gradient_warm_start` attribute that `MPPISolver` no longer has. The suite writes plots and a video into
`tests/result/` (ignored by git); steps 3 and 5 show them.

**Over SSH (no display).** The run ends in `5 passed, 1 skipped`, with two
`GLFWError` warnings (`The DISPLAY environment variable is missing`). The
skipped test is `test_gap_trajectory`'s video: MuJoCo renders through GLFW by
default, which needs a graphical session, and the test skips itself when it
cannot render. Render on the GPU through EGL instead, which needs no display:

```bash
MUJOCO_GL=egl PYTHONPATH=tests python -m pytest -q tests
```

This works the same in bash and fish, and the run then ends in
`6 passed, 1 warning`. The warning is `RuntimeWarning: os.fork() was called ...
JAX is multithreaded, so this will likely lead to a deadlock`: the video
writer starts `ffmpeg` as a subprocess, and Python warns about any fork in a
process that has JAX's threads running. The child process replaces itself with
`ffmpeg` immediately, so nothing can deadlock. If
you export `MUJOCO_GL=egl` for the whole session, a script that rendered may
print an `EGLError` traceback as Python exits; it comes from cleanup after the
rendering finished and can be ignored. Steps 1 to 8 open no windows, so they all
work over SSH; only `replay.py`, which opens MuJoCo's interactive viewer, needs
a real display.

**Lines you can ignore.** Every script first prints
`An NVIDIA GPU may be present on this machine, but a CUDA-enabled jaxlib is not
installed. Falling back to cpu.` and two `Failed to import warp` lines. JAX runs on
the CPU here, which is what the timings below assume. MuJoCo may also create
an untracked `MUJOCO_LOG.TXT` in `cmg/`. The outputs on these pages omit those lines.

## The steps

| Step | What it shows | Script | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1. The scene](01-scene.qmd) | `step.yaml` and `step.xml`: bodies, features, the 24 templates, tolerances | [`01_scene.py`](scripts/01_scene.py) | 2 s |
| [2. Templates and gaps](02-templates.qmd) | Every template's signed gap at one pose, and the band test | [`02_templates.py`](scripts/02_templates.py) | 3 s |
| [3. Formations](03-formations.qmd) | The band formation at seven named poses and along a 1,721-frame demo | [`03_formations.py`](scripts/03_formations.py) | 7 s |
| [4. The contact graph](04-graph.qmd) | Transfer-adjacent and shared-feature edges, and what is lost | [`04_graph.py`](scripts/04_graph.py) | 1 s |
| [5. The hold LP](05-hold.qmd) | Supported and EnvStable: the friction-cone LP behind the hold test | [`05_hold.py`](scripts/05_hold.py) | 23 s |
| [6. Candidate edits](06-candidates.qmd) | Which makes and breaks are legal at a node, and why | [`06_candidates.py`](scripts/06_candidates.py) | 26 s |
| [7. One solver call](07-mppi.qmd) | MPPI realizing one make, and how its result is judged | [`07_mppi.py`](scripts/07_mppi.py) | 2 min |
| [8. The search loop](08-search.qmd) | Two batches of breadth-first search, saving and loading the graph | [`08_search.py`](scripts/08_search.py), [`08b_search_rounds.py`](scripts/08b_search_rounds.py) | 2 min each |
| [9. Where step 1 starts](09-step1.qmd) | What the walkthrough exposed, mapped to the planar rewrite | none | none |

Times are wall-clock times on a 24-core CPU, including JAX compilation.
[`_common.py`](scripts/_common.py) holds shared helpers: the scene path, the
named poses, and readable template names such as `M:boundary-B:xn` (body:feature
on each side). [`replay.py`](scripts/replay.py) loops a trajectory in MuJoCo's
viewer if you have a display.

## What exists in the code

About 2,900 lines are implemented; the other 45 modules are stubs that hold only
a docstring describing their intended role.

| Layer | Implemented | Stub only |
|---|---|---|
| Scene | `scene/spec.py` (schema and YAML loader) | `scene/loader.py` |
| Geometry | `geometry/primitives.py` (3D gap kernels), `geometry/features.py` (faces, vertices, adjacency) | none |
| Catalog | `catalog/templates.py` (templates, `Catalog.gap`, `band`), `catalog/graph.py` (partial) | graph versioning |
| Marking | `marking/candidate.py` (`Cand`: legal edits) | `bitset.py`, `near.py`, `operators.py`, `statics.py` |
| Physics | `physics/world.py` (MJX world), `physics/hold.py` (support LP) | `mjx_backend.py` |
| Solver | `solver/mppi.py`, `solver/gradient.py` | `cem.py`, `success.py`, `cost/compiler.py` |
| Search | `search/__init__.py` (`Search`, `SearchState`, `Discretizer`, BFS ranker) | `engine.py`, `keys.py`, `node.py`, all four policies |
| Learning | none | `features/`, `model/`, `diffusion/`, `training/`, `calibration/` |
| Orchestration | none | `orchestration/` |

The roles of the stubbed marking modules are covered in practice by `Cand`
(step 6) and `physics/hold.py` (step 5). The learning and orchestration layers
are frozen by Decision 5, so this walkthrough does not visit them.
